title: §3/§4 — unfinished member blocks convergence; gates emit real disposition
goal: Suppress cycle convergence when any iteration member's disposition satisfies disposition_unfinished (§4/A), route router-terminated reason through router_reason_disposition in spec-coverage/spec-correspondence/review-report instead of hardcoding 'complete' (§3/B), and amend ADR-063 to Accepted on #2187's vocabulary (§C).

steps.description: Write the red tests for §4/A (must fail at merge-base). New integration test with a design_verify_cycle fixture: T1 — design returns disposition:timed_out + structurally valid design.md + design-gate pass + spec-coverage covered → the cycle does NOT converge that iteration (red: it converges today). T2 — same fixture with disposition:complete → cycle DOES converge (green baseline). T3 — at max_iterations with the last iteration member unfinished → cycle takes the exhaustion path, not complete.

Engine fix for §4/A: after the build-specific convergence suppression block at cycle-orchestrator.sh:2608-2613, add a second suppression that fires when converged==0 AND _iter_did_not_finish==1, emitting cycle.member_unfinished.suppressed_convergence. Update the comment at lines 2566-2573 which currently says '_iter_did_not_finish is Consumed ONLY by the reason-aware exhaustion halt' to reflect the new wider use. Keyed entirely on the disposition word via disposition_unfinished — no stage names.

Write the red tests for §3/B (must fail at merge-base, before the plugin fixes). Amend tests/unit/spec-coverage-test.sh: add SPEC-9 — when route_to_model exits non-zero (simulated timeout), the result has disposition:timed_out, NOT 'complete'. Amend tests/unit/spec-correspondence-test.sh: add a parallel SPEC — router timeout yields disposition from router_reason_disposition, not 'complete'. Amend tests/unit/review-report-v2-contract-test.sh (or review-report-plugin-test.sh): add a SPEC — when a lens rc file holds a non-zero router exit code, the stage's result disposition is the router_reason_disposition of that code, not 'complete'.

Fix spec-coverage for §3/B. In spec_coverage_run (plugin.sh:178-179), capture the router exit code before swallowing it: replace '|| true' with a local _scv_rc capture using a temp file. Parameterise _scv_write to accept a disposition argument (default 'complete'). In the 'no parseable verdict' branch (lines 192-195), when _scv_rc is non-zero, classify it via _router_rc_classify + router_reason_disposition and pass the resulting disposition word to _scv_write instead of letting it default to 'complete'.

Fix spec-correspondence for §3/B. In _sc_call (plugin.sh:98-118), accept an optional third argument — a path to a sink file — and write the raw router exit code to it when the router call exits non-zero (replace '|| true' with rc capture + conditional write). Parameterise _sc_write_result to accept a disposition argument (default 'complete'). In spec_correspondence_run, pass a temp file to _sc_call for the batch call, read back the rc, classify via _router_rc_classify + router_reason_disposition, and forward the disposition to _sc_write_result when the rc is non-zero.

Fix review-report for §3/B. In the failed-lens loop (plugin.sh:167-171), track the worst (numerically largest meaningful) non-zero rc across all failed lenses. After the loop, when _rr_failed_lenses is non-empty, classify the worst rc via _router_rc_classify + router_reason_disposition to get the disposition word; use that instead of the hardcoded 'complete' at line 174. Remove the stale #2187 comment that incorrectly justifies keeping 'complete'.

Amend ADR-063. Change Status to 'Accepted, amended 2026-09-30 by #2032'. In §3, replace every instance of 'exhausted' with 'timed_out'/'out_of_turns' and note the classifier is router_reason_disposition (scripts/lib/router-rc-classify.sh:259). In §4, strike the 'exhausted → escalate' half (retry + router-side timeout growth already replace it per ADR-029 and route.sh:872); keep and update the gate-fail-closed rule to reflect it is now implemented. In §1, replace 'One helper renders the budget block' with a note that the invariant is satisfied by per-stage _<stage>_budget_guidance helpers each reading the enforcing values. Add a dated back-pointer: 'Amended onto #2187's vocabulary; see #2187 for retirement of exhausted and escalate'.

notes:
ORDERING: steps 1 and 3 (red tests) must be committed before their corresponding implementation steps (2 and 4-6) so the PR body can state the assertion and how it failed at the merge-base. ADR amendment (step 7) can land last, after all tests are green.

CYCLE-ORCHESTRATOR INSERTION POINT: The new convergence suppression block goes between line 2613 (end of build-specific block) and line 2615 (start of #1265 no-committed-changes guard). The variable _iter_did_not_finish is already in scope and computed at lines 2574-2581. The check mirrors the build suppression: if [[ "$converged" -eq 0 ]] && [[ "$_iter_did_not_finish" -eq 1 ]]; then converged=1. This must NOT interfere with the empty_diff resting point: the empty_diff path sets all members' dispositions to 'complete', so disposition_unfinished returns false for all, _iter_did_not_finish stays 0, and the empty_diff case passes through correctly.

SPEC-CORRESPONDENCE RC CAPTURE: _sc_call is invoked via command substitution; shell semantics prevent a nameref from crossing the subshell boundary. A temp file written inside the subshell and read by the parent is the correct mechanism. The temp file should be cleaned up after the rc is read. Per-spec fallback calls also go through _sc_call; each should use its own sink file if needed, or only the batch call needs rc tracking (per-spec timeout is bounded by stage clock, not a new signal).

REVIEW-REPORT WORST-RC: The .rc files store raw router exit codes. 'Worst' can be defined as 'first non-zero found', since all non-zero codes classify to some unfinished disposition word via router_reason_disposition. A more principled ordering (timed_out > out_of_turns > others) is possible but out of scope; first-non-zero is sufficient to satisfy §3.

DESIGN-GATE: The issue notes design-gate never reads design's disposition and always writes disposition:complete. This is NOT in scope for this issue — §4/A fixes the engine (cycle-orchestrator) to block convergence when any member is unfinished, so design-gate does not need to change. design-gate's own disposition:complete is fine because it is a tool stage that did complete; it is design's timed_out disposition that should suppress convergence, and the engine fix handles that.

ADR-063 §2 (partial form): this is already done for design (#2186). No change needed.

BLOCKED-ON NOTE: The issue says blocked on #1835 (plan) and #1838 (impact), which are the last two stages on result_contract v1. This plan does NOT touch plan or impact; it only fixes spec-coverage, spec-correspondence, and review-report, which are already on v2. Verify this before implementing: spec-coverage-result.json and spec-correspondence-result.json both write result_contract:2 (confirmed in plugin.sh).

FIXTURE APPROACH FOR STEP 1: The test must drive the cycle-orchestrator directly (not a full pipeline run). Look at how tests/integration/cycle-on-max-pipeline-continues-test.sh and tests/integration/cycle-multi-iter-cumulative-test.sh construct their verdicts_blob fixtures — those are the reference pattern for stubbing member disposition values without a live LLM.
